unmapped_findings: 15Al alloy (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu, at.%) EDS-measured chemical composition (Table 1): Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 at.% (source b0012/b0013).

For the 15Al alloy, the optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness was mainly 525 °C–600 °C, and increasing Al content shifted this optimal range to higher temperatures (b0038).
For the 15Al alloy aged at 625 °C and 650 °C the hardness stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time; the 625 °C series plateau is near ~888 HV (b0037).

The paper's fracture-toughness (KIC), nanoindentation and TEM results were obtained on the peak-hardness 15Al condition (600 °C/6 h, 965.6 HV), not on the 625 °C/1 h sample; hence KIC (8.6 MPa·m^1/2), nanoindentation hardness (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa) and intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.1 ± 0.3 GPa) are not assigned to this sample (b0021, b0060, b0061).

β-Mn in the hardest 15Al sample had a composition of Mn 36.8 at.%, Al 14.3 at.%, Cu 2.8 at.%; increase of Al raised the Al dissolved in β-Mn and slightly enhanced its intrinsic hardness (b0060, b0067).
